findings.where: paper.tex Figure 3 caption (fig:hist8, line ~934): 'the bins refine the histogram of Section 6.4'
findings.description: Not quite: the figure's first bin (1, 21/20] merges three of Section 6.4's bins (37 in (1,1001/1000], 541 in (1001/1000,101/100], 2,777 in (101/100,21/20]; 37+541+2777 = 3,355). Only above 21/20 are the figure's bins a refinement. The counts are consistent, the wording is not.
findings.fix: Replace 'the bins refine the histogram of Section 6.4' by 'the bins are consistent with the histogram of Section 6.4 (coarser below 21/20, finer above)'.

findings.where: fig2_thresholds.pdf (Figure 5) and its caption: white streaks inside the n = 7 and n = 8 stacks
findings.description: The white horizontal streaks inside the n = 8 envelope and the n = 7 stack are real data: rows whose stable interval starts above q = 1 (lower end of kind root; 971 of the 9,133 at n = 8, sorted together because rows with equal upper ends are sorted by lower end). The caption describes the envelope but never says what the white gaps are, so a reader will take them for rendering artefacts. (At n = 8 the envelope is built by fill_betweenx, which interpolates linearly between consecutive rows, so a gap's ends are drawn as wedges spanning the neighbouring rows; at a row pitch of about 0.011 pt this is invisible, but it is why 'is what the dense stack ... would show' is true only up to sub-point interpolation.)
findings.fix: Add one clause to the caption, e.g. 'white gaps inside a stack are rows whose interval starts above q = 1 (971 of the 9,133 at n = 8)'; optionally draw the n = 8 stack with step='mid' (or as a LineCollection) so no interpolation between rows is involved.

findings.where: all figures, in-figure text sizes (make_figures.py rcParams: font.size 8, tick labels 7.5, fig5 bar counts 6.3 pt, fig3 annotation 6.8 pt)
findings.description: The figures are placed at \textwidth = 6.7 in, i.e. at 1:1, so the 6.3 pt rotated bar counts of Figure 3 and the 6.8 pt funnel annotation print at that size next to a 10.95 pt body; on the rendered page they are legible but noticeably small for print, and the right-hand panel's bars with counts 1-16 are sub-pixel, so those counts are carried by the small labels alone.
findings.fix: Raise the bar-count and annotation labels to at least 7 pt (and the base font to 9 pt), or drop the printed counts on the left panel, whose values are already in Table tab:n8edges.

findings.where: notes/paper/figures/ file names vs. figure numbers
findings.description: The file numbering does not follow the figure numbering in the paper: fig3_funnel.pdf is Figure 2, fig5_histograms.pdf is Figure 3, fig2_thresholds.pdf is Figure 5. Harmless, but confusing when a referee asks for 'Figure 2'.
findings.fix: Either rename the files to their figure numbers or leave as is; cosmetic.

findings.description: The label 'q_8^*(infinity) ~ 1.7107' ends 11 px from the right edge at 220 dpi (rightmost ink at column 1463 of 1474, about 1.3 mm). It is not clipped, but savefig is called without bbox_inches='tight', so any longer label (or a tick at a larger q) would be cut off silently.
findings.fix: Place the n = 8 label to the left of its tick (ha='right') or widen the axes' right margin.

findings.where: fig2_thresholds.pdf, q* ticks drawn at the midpoint of the stored isolating interval
findings.description: For q_6* the stored isolating interval (561/481, 7/6) has width 3.5e-4, so the tick sits 1.4e-4 q-units (about 0.001 in) to the right of the drawn upper ends of the two record rows; invisible at any print resolution, and the caption says 'at the midpoints of their isolating intervals', so this is correct as stated.
findings.fix: None needed; narrowing the q_6* interval the same way as the rows would make tick and row ends coincide exactly.

findings.description: The axis spans 6.3 data units (ylim -0.25 to 6.05), not 5.9, so the computed row pitch is 6.8 percent too large. With the clamp the n = 7 line width is 0.5 pt against a true pitch of 0.52 pt, so rows still do not overlap; no visual effect.
findings.fix: Use 6.3 (or compute the pitch from the axes transform) if the script is touched again.

findings.description: Bar length is log10(count), so bar lengths are not proportional to the counts (a 10^12 bar is only 3x a 10^4 bar). The caption states it and every count is printed, so it cannot be misread; an ordinal ramp on an ordered funnel is allowed by the anti-patterns file and reads correctly in grayscale.
findings.fix: None needed; a dot-and-label strip on a log axis would avoid the bar-length question entirely.
